c.tagline: Music City, USA — honky-tonks, hot chicken, and nonstop live music.

taxi.fareNote: Traditional taxis are metered, but ride-hailing (Uber/Lyft) is far more common and usually cheaper; street-hailing is rare outside downtown.

emergency.note: 911 is the single nationwide emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across the US.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Caution a few blocks off Broadway at night; petty crime in nightlife

hood_desc: Neon-lit honky-tonks, live music from morning to night, and the Ryman Auditorium pack Lower Broadway; loud, touristy, and the epicenter of Music City nightlife.
A polished, walkable district of rooftop bars, upscale restaurants, boutiques, and the famous wings mural; nightlife and dining in a modern high-rise setting.
An artsy, bohemian enclave across the river with vintage shops, indie coffee, dive bars, and some of the city's most creative kitchens; the local hipster heartland.
Nashville's oldest neighborhood, now a quiet, historic pocket of red-brick townhomes, acclaimed farm-to-table restaurants, and the Nashville Farmers' Market.
A trendy, photogenic strip of boutiques, brunch spots, and murals popular for shopping and strolling; leafy and residential just off the main drag.
lodging: Home2 Suites by Hilton Nashville Vanderbilt

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Buses generally run from about 5am to 11pm with reduced weekend frequency; the WeGo Star runs weekday peak hours only.
transit.pay: Buy fares in the WeGo app or pay cash on board (exact change). A local one-way bus ride is $2 and an all-day pass is $4. The WeGo Star commuter train to Lebanon has separate, zone-based fares.

transit.m: WeGo Route 18 airport bus to downtown (~30-45 min)

tip.r: ~15-20% at restaurants and bars is expected across the US; tipping is a core part of service workers' pay.
